source_text: Hic sit ergo summa certaminis: aut ostende imputatum sub lege fuisse cuiquam originale peccatum, ostende fuisse monstratum, et consentiam de hoc peccato Apostolum locutum fuisse.
pass_a_gloss: Let this therefore be the sum of the contest: either show that original sin was imputed under the law to anyone, show that it was shown, and I will consent that the Apostle spoke about this sin.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Let this, then, be the decisive issue: show that original sin was imputed to anyone under the law; show that it was revealed there; and I will agree that the apostle was speaking of this sin.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
